headline: Libertarian Scott Jewett calls on Donalds, Jolly to debate in Florida governor's race
teaser: Libertarian gubernatorial candidate Scott Jewett is calling on Republican Byron Donalds and Democrat David Jolly to share a debate stage with him as Florida's general election approaches.
body:
Libertarian candidate Scott Jewett is challenging Republican nominee Byron Donalds and Democratic nominee David Jolly to debate him ahead of Florida's Nov. 3 gubernatorial election.

Jewett said he wants voters to hear the candidates address affordability, property taxes, homeowners insurance, housing and economic policy on the same stage.

Jewett and running mate Nicole Skelly are qualified for the general-election ballot. Donalds and Jolly won their respective Republican and Democratic primaries in August. Several additional non-major-party candidates are also qualified for the governor's race.

The challenge comes as efforts to arrange debates between Donalds and Jolly have stalled. Jolly said in September that he would not participate in debates with Donalds, citing the tone of the campaign and what he described as bad-faith attacks. Donalds has criticized that decision and continued calling for debates.

Recent polling has shown relatively narrow margins between the two major-party nominees. A St. Pete Polls survey conducted Sept. 15-17 found Donalds at 43.5% and Jolly at 43.4%, with 8.9% undecided and 4.3% selecting someone else.

A Change Research survey conducted Sept. 7-9 found Jolly at 47% and Donalds at 44%, while an August Hart Research Associates poll conducted for the Democratic Governors Association found Jolly at 46% and Donalds at 45%.

Those polls primarily measured the contest between Donalds and Jolly and did not report Jewett as a named candidate in their main results.

Jewett pointed to Florida's 2018 gubernatorial election as an example of how narrow statewide races can become. Republican Ron DeSantis defeated Democrat Andrew Gillum by 32,463 votes, 49.59% to 49.19%.

“The polling shows just how closely divided Florida can be,” Jewett said. “When the two major-party candidates are separated by only a few points — or fractions of a point — the voters looking for an alternative can have an enormous impact on the direction of this state.”

Jewett's campaign said it is seeking opportunities for the candidates to appear together at university forums. The campaign release listed Stetson University, Florida A&M University and Florida Atlantic University.

Public schedules do not fully match the dates listed in the campaign release. Stetson has an Oct. 5 candidate forum on its calendar, while Florida Atlantic University has an Oct. 15 gubernatorial debate publicly announced. Florida A&M had announced a gubernatorial debate for Sept. 29 rather than the Oct. 12 date cited by Jewett's campaign.

“Come debate me,” Jewett said. “Let's stand on the same stage, take the same questions and explain what we would actually do as Governor. Then let Florida voters decide.”

Florida's general election is Nov. 3.
